title: Louisiana's 2nd Congressional District election, 2026
description: The election for Louisiana's 2nd Congressional District is in flux after the U.S. Supreme Court struck down the state's congressional map as an unconstitutional racial gerrymander in Louisiana v. Callais (April 2026). Incumbent Democrat Troy Carter, who has held the seat since 2021, faces a primary challenge from Renada Collins, but the May 2026 primary was suspended by Governor Jeff Landry pending map redrawing. The district, which stretches from New Orleans to Baton Rouge, is rated Solid/Safe Democratic by major nonpartisan forecasters. The final candidate slate and election calendar remain uncertain as state lawmakers work to adopt new district boundaries.
polling_note: No public opinion polls were found for this race as of mid-2026.

candidates.name: Troy Carter
candidates.summary: Troy Carter is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Louisiana's 2nd Congressional District, first elected in a 2021 special election. He previously served in the Louisiana State Senate (as Minority Leader), the New Orleans City Council, and the Louisiana House of Representatives. Carter is a Democrat and one of two Democrats in Louisiana's congressional delegation.

candidates.name: Renada Collins
candidates.summary: Renada Collins is a Democratic candidate challenging incumbent Troy Carter in the primary for Louisiana's 2nd Congressional District. She ran as an independent candidate for mayor of New Orleans in 2025 and has worked as a TV host at Bigg Mouth Media Group since 2016. Ballotpedia notes her career experience also includes serving as a banking executive.

forecast.rationale: No public polling exists for this race. The Supreme Court's April 2026 ruling in Louisiana v. Callais struck down the current congressional map as an unconstitutional racial gerrymander, forcing a redraw. The May 2026 primary was suspended by Gov. Jeff Landry, leaving the candidate field, district lines, and election calendar uncertain. Despite this procedural turbulence, the district's core — anchored in heavily Democratic areas of New Orleans and Baton Rouge — has been rated Solid/Safe Democratic by major nonpartisan forecasters. Incumbent Democrat Troy Carter is the strongest candidate in the field, while his only listed challenger (Renada Collins, also a Democrat) ran an unsuccessful independent mayoral bid in 2025. No Republican candidates have filed. However, a redrawn map could shift district boundaries in ways that modestly alter the partisan composition, tempering confidence. Democrats remain clear favorites with a likely-d rating, as the district is almost certain to stay Democratic regardless of map changes, but the redistricting process injects meaningful uncertainty that prevents a safe-d rating.
